Parents who had sold sons, tens and hundreds, waited on the road, and not one young son was seen going off with the wicked eunuch; none failed to shed tears, grieving that their sons must have been cooked.

paragraphs.zh: 按：貧民賣子，極為至愚。若不能養，何不若鳳陽府父子俱丐，猶可骨肉相保。必不得已，唯可賣之富戶為僕。固不可供太監之啖，亦不可賣入庵寺為行童侍者，其賤尤在乞丐下也。國家置閹尹，以供掃除傳命耳。至使握利權，享用已極，更思生陽物淫婦人，為不可必得之事。雖食人而可為汝欲扶已朽之軀，曾不惜人渾全之命乎？是可忍也，孰不可忍也！孟子曰：「善戰者服上刑」，猶為強兵而殺人也；此為何事而視人命如草菅乎？王法若明，當不令此閹得生還矣。
paragraphs.en: Note: Poor people selling sons is the height of folly. If you cannot raise them, why not, like Fengyang prefecture, father and son both beg, still keeping flesh and bone together? If you must, you may only sell them to a rich house as servants. You must not supply a eunuch’s eating, nor sell them into convents and temples as novices and attendants—that is even lower than beggars. The state sets eunuchs to sweep and pass orders. To let them grasp the profit-power, enjoy to the extreme, then think of growing an organ to debauch women—a thing they cannot possibly get. Even if eating people could prop up your already rotten body for your desire, would you not spare a person’s whole life? If this can be borne, what cannot be borne! Mencius said “those good at war should suffer the heaviest punishment”—still, that is killing people for a strong army; for what business is this, treating human life as grass? If the king’s law were clear, this eunuch should not have been allowed to return alive.

stories.title_en: A Fake Face-to-Face Bribe to the Education Intendant

paragraphs.zh: 凡学道出巡，各处棍徒云集追随，专体探富家子有谋钻刺者，多方献门路，以图蛊骗。或此路不售，后一帮又生一端以投，年年有堕其术者。但受骗之家羞以告人，故后次人又蹈之。
paragraphs.en: Whenever the education intendant goes on tour, swindlers from all around gather and follow, specially probing for rich men’s sons who want to drill connections. They offer openings in many ways, hoping to cheat. If this path does not sell, another gang then produces another angle to pitch; every year some fall for it. But families who are cheated are ashamed to tell others, so the next people step in again.

paragraphs.zh: 有一学道，考选至公，不纳分上。忽一棍自言能通于道者，人不之信。棍曰：“此道爷自开私门，最不喜人央分上前途。唯对手干者，百发百中，但人不敢耳。如真肯干者，但要现钱，彼当面接之，可稳保成就。”赵甲问曰：“从何处献之？”棍曰：“候退堂后，先用手本开具某县某人银若干，求取进学。彼肯面允，便进上银；如不允，银在我手，彼奈我何？”赵甲曰：“我要在旁亲看。”棍曰：“自然与你亲看。学道的二门，其缝阔一寸，从外窥之，直见堂上，任你看之。”赵甲曰：“若道肯亲手接银，吾敢投之。”即写手本，以手帕包银二百两作一封。
paragraphs.en: There was an education intendant, fair in examining and selecting, who took no private requests. Suddenly a swindler claimed he could get through to the intendant; people did not believe him. The swindler said: “This Intendant opened a private door himself; he most dislikes people asking for introductions ahead. Only those who deal with him directly succeed every time—people just don’t dare. If you truly will do it, you only need ready money; he’ll take it face to face; success can be firmly guaranteed.” Zhao Jia asked: “Where do we present it?” The swindler said: “Wait till he leaves the hall; first use a name-card listing such-and-such county, so-and-so, so much silver, asking to be taken into the school. If he agrees in person, then present the silver; if he doesn’t, the silver is in my hands—what can he do to me?” Zhao Jia said: “I want to stand beside and watch myself.” The swindler said: “Of course you’ll watch yourself. The second gate of the education office has a crack an inch wide; peeking from outside you can see straight to the hall; watch as you like.” Zhao Jia said: “If the intendant will take the silver with his own hands, I’ll dare to go in.” He wrote a name-card and wrapped two hundred taels in a kerchief as one packet.

paragraphs.zh: 下午出堂，往道前候之。棍曰：“要二包过门银。”甲付与之。将退堂之际，棍以银与手本挨入堂去，嘱甲曰：“才封门时，即要在门缝来看。”及道退堂后，甲于二门缝中看，见道仍旧纱帽圆领而出。棍先以手本高递上，一门子接进。道展看了，笼入袖中去。棍又高擎一封银上，道顾门子，门子接上银。道一看即转身，门子随后捧银包而入。棍趋至二门，隔门谓甲曰：“好了，好了，事已妥矣！你见否？”甲应曰：“我亲见了，果是自接。”棍曰：“今夜不能出，我你须在门内外宿矣。”甲曰：“但得事妥，不吃晚饭亦好。”
paragraphs.en: In the afternoon they went out to wait before the office. The swindler said: “Need two packets of gate-passing silver.” Jia paid him. As the session was about to end, the swindler took the silver and name-card and squeezed into the hall, and told Jia: “As soon as they seal the gate, come look through the crack.” After the intendant left the hall, Jia looked through the second-gate crack and saw the intendant still in gauze cap and round collar come out. The swindler first held the name-card high; a page took it in. The intendant opened and looked, and tucked it in his sleeve. The swindler then held a packet of silver high; the intendant glanced at the page; the page took up the silver. The intendant glanced and turned; the page followed in with the silver packet. The swindler hurried to the second gate and said through the door: “Good, good, it’s done! Did you see?” Jia said: “I saw it myself; he did take it himself.” The swindler said: “Tonight I can’t go out; you and I must sleep inside and outside the gate.” Jia said: “If the matter is settled, going without supper is fine.”

paragraphs.zh: 次日开早门，棍与甲方同出，即到甲店拜贺。甲大设席待之。棍曰：“高取后须厚谢我。”甲曰：“加一谢是定规，不加亦不减矣。”此为信棍之戒。
paragraphs.en: The next day the early gate opened; the swindler and Jia went out together and went to Jia’s inn to congratulate. Jia set a big feast. The swindler said: “After you place high you must thank me generously.” Jia said: “Ten percent thanks is the fixed rule; I won’t add or subtract.” This is a warning against trusting swindlers.

paragraphs.zh: 后揭晓日，本生无名。棍查不见踪，方知前受银之道，乃此棍先与宿衙人套定，盖妆假道也。
paragraphs.en: On results day, this candidate’s name was not there. The swindler was nowhere to be found; only then they knew the “intendant” who took the silver was this swindler, who had first arranged with the night-duty yamen men to dress up as a fake intendant.

paragraphs.zh: 二门望入堂上，虽可亲见，终是路遥，哪见得真？故落此棍骗而不知。若真道自接银，何必衣冠出？何必堂上递手本？又何必堂上交银？独不可私递手本乎？况堂上有宿衙人役，岂私受银之地？此村富不识官体，故以目见为稳，不知与你目见，正所以骗你也。
paragraphs.en: Looking from the second gate into the hall, though you can see it yourself, the way is still long—how can you see truly? So they fell for this swindle without knowing. If a real intendant took silver himself, why come out in full dress? Why present a name-card in the hall? Why hand over silver in the hall? Couldn’t the name-card be passed privately? Besides, the hall has night-duty staff; how is it a place to take silver in private? This rustic rich man did not know official form, so he took seeing with his eyes as secure; he did not know that letting you see with your eyes was exactly how they cheated you.

stories.title_en: Sealed Silver in a Retired Official’s Inner Room

paragraphs.zh: 富人钱一，欲为子买进学。歇家孙丙，有意骗之，与之言曰：“此中李乡官，原与学道同僚，二人极相得。今若说一名进学，此断可得。吾试与商议之。”钱一曰：“可。”孙丙往匠铺，见两挂箱一样，用钱三钱买其一，又以银二分定后只，嘱曰：“我停会引人来买，更出三钱，不可别换。”又买两把一样的锁。后以挂箱与锁付李乡官家人曰：“你可秤定二百两石头，装在挂箱内，外加锁之，放在你家主房内。少顷，我领人央你老爷说进学，以二百两好银与你封。你把放银的箱收入，换放石的箱出来，然后将这银与我均分。”李家人许曰：“可。”
paragraphs.en: Rich man Qian Yi wanted to buy his son into the school. Innkeeper Sun Bing meant to cheat him, and said: “Official Li here was once a colleague of the education intendant; the two are very close. If we speak for one name into the school, it’s certainly available. Let me try discussing it.” Qian Yi said: “All right.” Sun Bing went to a carpenter’s shop, saw two hanging cases alike, bought one for three qian, and with two fen reserved the later one, telling them: “In a bit I’ll bring someone to buy; he’ll pay another three qian; don’t swap another.” He also bought two identical locks. Then he gave a hanging case and lock to Official Li’s servant: “Weigh out two hundred taels of stones, put them in the hanging case, lock it outside, put it in your master’s room. Shortly I’ll bring someone asking your lord to speak for entering school, with two hundred taels of good silver for you to seal. You take in the case with silver, bring out the case with stones, then split this silver with me.” Li’s servant agreed: “All right.”

paragraphs.zh: 孙丙领李家人来，对钱一说：“我面见李老爷了，他道此事容易，只把现银对于他家人看过锁住，送到他家加封条，仍以银箱付还我，以锁匙付他收。待有名进学之后，将原银谢他，不得开箱再换。”钱一曰：“在你家借一挂箱来用。”孙丙曰：“新锁有，挂箱可往街买之。”领钱一家人，以银三钱，往铺买到。钱一将银二百两同李家人、孙丙三面对定，收入挂箱中，外加锁定。
paragraphs.en: Sun Bing brought Li’s servant and told Qian Yi: “I saw Lord Li in person; he said this is easy; just have ready silver shown to his servant, locked, sent to his house for a sealing strip, then the silver case is returned to me, the key given to him to keep. After the name is on the list for the school, the original silver is his thanks; the case must not be opened and swapped.” Qian Yi said: “I’ll borrow a hanging case at your place.” Sun Bing said: “There’s a new lock; the hanging case can be bought on the street.” He led one of Qian’s people, paid three qian, and bought it at the shop. Qian Yi, with Li’s servant and Sun Bing, the three facing, put two hundred taels in the hanging case and locked it outside.

paragraphs.zh: 孙丙负银，同钱一到李乡官家，求加封条。李乡官推病，在厅左房内坐。李家人持箱入门边曰：“银已看对阴白，只讨一封条。”李乡官曰：“既看明白，还他自收，来接封条。”李家人仍以银箱出，再领出一封条，对三面封讫。钱一解锁匙，付李家人收。孙丙复负银箱归，交与钱一自收藏，皆谓事极妥矣。
paragraphs.en: Sun Bing carried the silver, went with Qian Yi to Official Li’s, asking for a sealing strip. Official Li claimed illness and sat in the room left of the hall. Li’s servant held the case at the door: “The silver has been checked, yin-white; we only ask one sealing strip.” Official Li said: “Since it’s been checked clearly, give it back for him to keep, and come get the sealing strip.” Li’s servant still brought the silver case out, then brought out a sealing strip, and sealed it before the three. Qian Yi unlocked and gave the key to Li’s servant. Sun Bing carried the silver case back and gave it to Qian Yi to keep; all thought the matter extremely secure.

paragraphs.zh: 及揭晓，钱一子无名。孙丙曰：“事不成，银现在，可速收拾归，免得李家人来索轿价。”钱一既失望，怏怏而归。及到半路，叫匠人开锁启视，则皆石头矣。惊异复回，大闹歇家曰：“你何通同骗我？”孙丙曰：“我与你当面干事，何处是骗你？若三面共开挂箱，犹怪得李家；今去半日，私自开箱，我那知中间是银是石？”钱一明知是孙、李合骗，只事无凭证，谅是难取，但辱骂歇家一场而归。此为信乡官之戒。
paragraphs.en: When results were posted, Qian Yi’s son had no name. Sun Bing said: “It didn’t work; the silver is still here; pack up and go home quickly, lest Li’s people come asking sedan fees.” Qian Yi, disappointed, went home dejected. Halfway he called a carpenter to open the lock and look: all stones. Shocked, he went back and made a big row at the inn: “How did you collude to cheat me?” Sun Bing said: “I did the business with you face to face; where was the cheat? If the three had opened the hanging case together, you could still blame the Li house; now after half a day’s travel you privately opened the case; how would I know whether inside was silver or stone?” Qian Yi knew well it was Sun and Li cheating together, but there was no proof; he figured it was hard to recover, only insulted the innkeeper a round and went home. This is a warning against trusting retired officials.

paragraphs.zh: 按：两挂箱共样，本是难辨。但加封条，只须在外封之，何必持入内禀乃请封条乎？向令当时若告，追究卖挂箱之家，问两箱何以一样，或能证出孙丙先买其一，后领人买一。或遇明官，便可从中勘出换包之骗矣。
paragraphs.en: Note: Two hanging cases of the same pattern are originally hard to tell apart. But adding a sealing strip only needed to be done outside; why take it inside to report and then request the strip? If at the time one had sued, investigating the shop that sold hanging cases, asking why two cases were alike, one might prove Sun Bing first bought one, then led someone to buy one. Meeting a clear official, the swap-the-package cheat could be found out from this.

paragraphs.zh: 建宁府郝天广，世家巨富，有几所庄，多系白米。时建宁无价，其智家罗五闻省城米价高腾，邀主人带二仆，以米十馀船装往省粜。时宗主王爷发牌考延、建二府，各有告示，将考儒童。米才上船，有一客人带二仆，来搭船往省。船中暇坐，问其何干。答曰：“王爷家来投书者。”后又谈及可夤缘之事，天广有长子出考，言甚合意；只宗主前考甚公，并无私窦，未敢深信其事。
paragraphs.en: Hao Tianguang of Jianning prefecture came from a hereditary rich family, with several estates, mostly white rice. At the time Jianning had no good price; his steward Luo Wu heard rice prices in the provincial capital were soaring, invited the master with two servants, and loaded ten-odd boats of rice to sell in the capital. At that time His Honor the education commissioner Wang had issued a notice examining Yan and Jian prefectures; there were proclamations that boy-students would be examined. Rice just loaded, a guest with two servants came to catch the boat to the capital. Sitting at leisure on the boat, they asked what his business was. He answered: “Coming from His Honor Wang’s household to deliver a letter.” Later they talked of things one might pull strings for. Tianguang had an eldest son sitting the exam; the talk suited him well; only the commissioner had examined very fairly last time, with no private hole, so he did not quite dare believe.

paragraphs.zh: 至省中，棍辞别去，曰：“王爷有公子在学，必共看卷。试与谈尊府事，倘许诺，我再出回你诺；若不出，则事不谐耳，再亦无信。”天广曰：“是也。”密遣一仆，踪迹棍所去处，果入学道衙去。数日后出来曰：“事谐矣。可将银对定，以我皮箱藏之，外加封条，银仍与你自收掌。后有名进学，即以皮箱银交出与我。”天广思“银虽对定，仍是我藏，有何不可？”即依言对讫，不知此棍有甚法。银明是天广自投自锁，棍只加封票一条而去，再约曰：“今夜间公子或可潜出，我与之同看过，事即美矣。”连候数夜不来，天广以皮箱开看，其内尽是砖石，前银已被赚去矣。此为封银防换之戒。
paragraphs.en: At the provincial capital the swindler took leave: “His Honor Wang has a young master in the school; they must look at papers together. I’ll try talking about your honorable house; if he agrees, I’ll come out and tell you the yes; if I don’t come out, the matter isn’t on; there will be no further word.” Tianguang said: “Right.” He secretly sent a servant to track where the swindler went; indeed he entered the education office. After several days he came out: “It’s arranged. Weigh out the silver, hide it in my leather case, add a sealing strip outside; the silver stays in your own keeping. After the name is on the list for school, you hand the leather case of silver to me.” Tianguang thought, “Though the silver is checked, I still keep it—what’s wrong with that?” He followed, checked it out, not knowing what method this swindler had. The silver was clearly put in and locked by Tianguang himself; the swindler only added one sealing ticket and left, and further agreed: “Tonight the young master may slip out; I’ll look it over with him, and the matter will be fine.” They waited several nights; he did not come. Tianguang opened the leather case: all bricks and stones; the former silver had been cheated away. This is a warning: when sealing silver, guard against a swap.

paragraphs.zh: 按：买进学、买帮补，甚至买举人，此事处处有之，岁岁有之，而建宁一府，叠遭骗害为甚。盖建郡民富财多，性浮轻轻故也。虽累受骗，而继起营买者未已，此光棍途中常以逢考建宁为一桩好生意也。特其封银法，至今人看不破。明以银与之同封，复还我收，及棍去后开之，则皆砖石矣；或以为有一遁银法。如此神矣哉，上智难防也！唯明鉴乎此，勿信为上。若急欲买进，可勿封银，须以榜上有名为定。若只信其漏报，虽至三四次见金榜矣，亦未可以银付之，方可防其脱也。
paragraphs.en: Note: Buying entry to school, buying a stipend place, even buying a juren—this happens everywhere, every year, and Jianning prefecture has suffered stacked cheats worst. Because Jian commandery people are rich, with much wealth, and their nature is flighty and light. Though repeatedly cheated, those who then rise to buy still don’t stop; so swindlers on the road often treat the Jianning exams as a good line of business. Especially the method of sealing silver: to this day people can’t see through it. Clearly you seal the silver together, it’s given back for you to keep, and after the swindler leaves you open it—all bricks and stones; some think there’s a method of making silver vanish. How miraculous—even the wisest can hardly guard against it! Only see this clearly; not believing is best. If you urgently want to buy entry, don’t seal silver; take a name on the posted list as the settlement. If you only believe his leaked reports, even if you see the golden list three or four times, you still must not hand over silver; only then can you guard against being stripped.

stories.title_en: Sealing Silver in an Empty House, Then a Staged Robbery

paragraphs.zh: 骗局多端，唯仕进一途，竟奔者多，故遭骗者众。棍尝有言，唯虚名可骗实利，唯虚声可赚实物。盖仕进之人，求名之心胜，虽掷重利不暇顾惜，遂入棍术中而不及察。
paragraphs.en: Swindles have many forms; only the path of official advancement has many who rush it, so many are cheated. Swindlers have a saying: only an empty name can cheat solid profit; only empty sound can earn solid goods. Because people seeking office have a heart that wants a name so strong, they throw down heavy profit without time to care, and so enter the swindler’s art without examining.

paragraphs.zh: 有一巨富家子，欲营谋进学，所带管家者极为能干。往省考大续，寓一歇家中，令其求关通之路。数日内，以门路投者，更进迭来。管家者窥其行径，穷其来历，皆察其言事不相应，踪迹不分明，多与歇家有套同情弊，悉拒却之，不信其哄。后一棍妆为仆价，言语迟钝，举动村朴，自方跟一罢职乡官，与宗主有旧，来此打秋风。引管家去见乡官，果似贫薄小官样。面酌定一名进学，只谢银一百两亦肯讲，只要现银，来伊店封。管家曰：“在我店封。”乡官曰：“事宜慎密，你店内人众，传扬不便。此下有一所空房，是顾秀才的，前欲在彼借寓，以借什物不便，故迁在此。可与我小价在彼处封定，最是稳当。”管家强求乡官来所住店看封为妥。乡官曰：“汝更有疑，我只小价一人，任你多用人来同封。”管家回以“外人不可与知，只同本主去。”果只村仆一人在，把银出对定。忽有棍数人，打开门入曰：“汝辈买秀才，吾拿去出首！”将三人打倒，银尽抢去。
paragraphs.en: A very rich family’s son wanted to scheme for school entry; the steward he brought was extremely capable. Going to the provincial capital for the student examination, they lodged at an inn and told him to seek a connecting path. Within days, people offering openings came one after another. The steward watched their conduct, traced their origins, saw their words and affairs didn’t match, their tracks unclear, many in collusion with the inn—he refused them all, didn’t believe the talk. Later a swindler dressed as a servant, slow of speech, rustic in manner, claiming he followed a dismissed retired official who had old ties with the commissioner, come here to seek gifts. He led the steward to see the official; indeed he looked like a poor minor official. They agreed face to face on one name for school; even a hundred taels as thanks he’d discuss, but it had to be ready silver, sealed at his inn. The steward said: “Seal at my inn.” The official said: “The matter should be discreet; your inn has many people, inconvenient if it spreads. Below there’s an empty house, Xiucai Gu’s; I wanted to lodge there before, but borrowing furnishings was inconvenient, so I moved here. You and my little servant can seal it there; that’s most secure.” The steward strongly asked the official to come to the inn they stayed at to watch the sealing. The official said: “If you still doubt, I have only one little servant; you may send as many people as you like to seal together.” The steward replied, “Outsiders mustn’t know; I’ll only go with my master.” Indeed only the rustic servant was there; they brought out silver and checked it. Suddenly several swindlers broke in the door: “You people are buying a xiucai; we’ll seize you and report it!” They knocked the three down and robbed all the silver.

paragraphs.zh: 村仆爬起，做烦恼样。管家起，挈其手曰：“不须恼，此银亦不多，同在我店再封。”村仆不肯去。富子曰：“事已错矣，何可再干？”管家曰：“我自有处。”强邀村仆再来，一面令富子速收拾回家。管家雇募店中人，将自己当作儒士，与村仆对锁，送入县中，口告被脱抢之故。县官曰：“你不合买进学，与者受者各有其罪。况被棍抢银，与乡官家人何干？”管家曰：“抢银者即此棍之伙。但穷究此银出，情愿追入官；更愿大罚，与此棍同罪。”县官再差人去叫乡官，早已走了。县官曰：“此果是棍。”严刑拷打。棍仆受刑不过，愿赔一半。追完，管家又告愿全追，甘与同配驿。棍仆死不肯摊出同伙；又累受刑，无可追。乃将棍仆拟徒，管家者只拟杖发归。此为封银防抢之戒。
paragraphs.en: The rustic servant crawled up, putting on a distressed look. The steward got up, took his hand, and said: “Don’t worry; this silver isn’t much; come to my inn and we’ll seal again.” The servant wouldn’t go. The rich son said: “The matter has already gone wrong; how can we do it again?” The steward said: “I have a way.” He forced the servant to come again, and on one side told the rich son to pack up and go home quickly. The steward hired people from the inn, passed himself off as a Confucian student, locked himself with the rustic servant, sent them into the county, and orally reported being stripped and robbed. The county magistrate said: “You shouldn’t have bought school entry; giver and receiver each have their crime. Besides, being robbed by swindlers—what’s it to the retired official’s servant?” The steward said: “The robbers were this swindler’s gang. Only thoroughly investigate where this silver went; I’m willing to have it recovered for the government; I’m also willing to be heavily fined, same crime as this swindler.” The magistrate then sent people to call the retired official; he had already fled. The magistrate said: “This is indeed a swindler.” Harsh torture. The servant-swindler couldn’t bear the punishment, and was willing to repay half. After it was chased in, the steward again sued, wanting the whole recovered, willing to share penal exile to a post-station. The servant-swindler would die rather than name his gang; tortured again, nothing more to chase. So they sentenced the servant-swindler to penal servitude, the steward only to beating and sent home. This is a warning: when sealing silver, guard against robbery.

paragraphs.zh: 按：管家虽有能，终落棍所脱抢。特既抢后，即能拿棍仆同解，甘与同罪，终能追其一半，棍亦无所利。若富子自己，必不肯与棍同罪，而一抢之后，无如之何矣。或曰：管家顶认儒士，若官考之何如？曰：央分上之人，已是天才，官何须考？即考不得，亦无妨也。
paragraphs.en: Note: Though the steward had ability, he still fell to the swindlers’ robbery. But after the robbery he could seize the servant-swindler and go together, willing to share the crime, and in the end recover half; the swindlers also got no profit. If it had been the rich son himself, he surely wouldn’t share a crime with the swindler, and after one robbery there would be nothing to be done. Some say: the steward posed as a Confucian student; what if the official examined him? Answer: a person asking for private introductions is already a genius; why would the official need to examine? Even if he failed an exam, it wouldn’t matter.

stories.title_en: Posing as a Patronage-Seeker to Collect Bribes

paragraphs.zh: 简学宪最廉明。考大续时，有秋风客到，寓于开明僧舍。次日，有一棍带三仆来，亦与同寓。内中相拜，自称彼系县堂亲眷，亦来打秋风者。外则炫耀冠服，仆从扔卫更盛，每与（冠）盖往来寺中。尝有生儒遇之，辄误指曰：“此学道乡亲也。”又见简道亲回拜，又请酒，偕真秋风客往，而棍专外影窃其名，以欺诳人。简公是严明人，不数日，真秋风客已打发行矣，唯棍在寺。其外棍伙故四下传扬曰：“学爷乡亲在某寺。”生儒中亦甚传之，多有求取大续者，只无人可担当银。棍背套学道衙中书手、皂隶来，过付银封于其家。人既信是真秋风客，又衙门有身役人与同事，银封其家，亦复何虑？棍客动云，彼要说十名，每名要三百两。当赴场人众，各务兢趋，数日已满十人之数。共日封于各书、皂之家，明白交付，共银三千两。背地各瓜分已讫。
paragraphs.en: Education Intendant Jian was most honest and clear. During the student examination, a patronage-seeker arrived, lodging at Kaiming monks’ quarters. The next day a swindler with three servants also lodged there. They exchanged visits; he claimed to be a relative of the county hall, also come to seek gifts. Outside he displayed caps and robes; servants and guards even more splendid; often went back and forth in the temple with official canopies. Students who met him often mistook: “This is the education intendant’s country relative.” They also saw Intendant Jian’s relative return the visit, and invite to wine; he went along with the real patronage-seeker, while the swindler specialized in stealing that name from the outside to deceive people. Lord Jian was a strict, clear man; within days the real patronage-seeker had been sent off; only the swindler remained at the temple. His outside gang deliberately spread around: “The Intendant’s country relative is at such-and-such temple.” Among students it was much passed on; many seeking the examination had no one to take charge of the silver. The swindler had secretly arranged with clerks and runners of the education office to come, and pass sealed silver at their homes. People already believed he was the real patronage-seeker, and yamen staff with posts were in on it; silver sealed at their homes—what further worry? The swindler-guest kept saying he would speak for ten names, three hundred taels each. With many going to the field, each competing to rush, within days the ten were full. That day they sealed at various clerks’ and runners’ homes, delivered clearly, three thousand taels in all. Behind the scenes they had already split it.

paragraphs.zh: 但思后日无名，不能回复诸人，银亦何以得去？乃雇一人，往学道出首：“见得衙门书、皂某某等，外同客棍招揽生童银若干两，封于某某等家。”简准状，即出白牌，提拿客棍风火至急，秋风棍即乘机逃去。又拿在衙书皂拶夹，皆不肯招，各打三十，革役。又差人往衙役家搜缉。凡有名与列钻刺者，闻踪迹露出，唯恐指名逮捕，各各四散，走回本县，银都弃撇，不敢来问。由是棍得安享所分之银。书皂虽革役，无赃可据，后复陆续谋入。唯一时受夹打，彼刑用在衙人役，亦仅如搬戏；而所得之多，奚止偿失也！此为信秋风客之戒。
paragraphs.en: But they thought: later when there’s no name, they can’t answer people, and how can the silver get away? So they hired someone to go to the education office and report: “Clerks and runners so-and-so of the yamen, together with an outside guest-swindler, solicited so much silver from students, sealed at so-and-so’s homes.” Jian accepted the complaint, issued a plain warrant, to seize the guest-swindler with fire-and-wind urgency; the patronage swindler then used the chance to flee. Then they seized the yamen clerks and runners, squeezed and pressed; none would confess; each beaten thirty, dismissed. Then sent people to search the yamen men’s homes. Anyone named as having drilled for a place, hearing their tracks were out, feared being named and arrested, scattered in all directions, fled back to their counties, abandoned the silver, dared not come ask. Thus the swindler could enjoy in peace the silver he’d split. The clerks and runners though dismissed, no stolen goods could be proven; later they gradually schemed their way back in. They only suffered squeezing and beating for a time; using punishment on yamen staff is also only like putting on a play; and what they got was more than enough to repay the loss! This is a warning against trusting patronage-seekers.

paragraphs.zh: 按：此棍称学道乡亲，而学道既已来拜，又请吃酒，则的是乡亲矣。况书、皂皆有身役人，为之翼护，人孰疑之？不知真乡亲已去，而此乃其托名者。彼衙门人唯利是图，所敛既多，何惜数十之板？况其顶头银仍在，虽革役，乌足以惩之。今人谓衙役知法，不知侮法者正是知法之人。唯蹈实地行实事，以真学问博真功名，勿萌侥幸，勿图钻刺，棍骗何从入哉？彼遭骗者，皆惰学不肖之徒，自取灾眚者也。
paragraphs.en: Note: This swindler claimed to be the education intendant’s country relative, and the intendant had already come to visit and invited him to drink, so he truly was a country relative. Besides, clerks and runners all had posts, shielding him—who would suspect? They didn’t know the real relative had gone, and this was one borrowing the name. Those yamen men only seek profit; having collected so much, why begrudge a few dozen strokes? Besides their post-purchase silver is still there; even dismissed, how is that enough to punish them? People today say yamen runners know the law; they don’t know those who insult the law are exactly people who know the law. Only walk on solid ground, do solid things, win a true name with true learning; don’t sprout luck-seeking, don’t plot drilling—how would swindles get in? Those who are cheated are all lazy, unworthy students who bring disaster on themselves.

stories.title_en: Silver Left with an Innkeeper Is Stolen

paragraphs.zh: 有三棍合帮，共骗得银三百两，未肯遂分，更留合装骗棚，以图大骗。先遣一人过省，离会城两日之府，用银七十两买屋，内系土库，城外铺舍开一客店。又用银五十两娶一妻，买一婢，又买一家奴。更有数十两在手上，调度供家。人见其店有家着奴婢，食用丰足，多往宿其店。此府相近省城，往年文宗考科举不及，常调邻府生童到此合考，以便往返，每富家生童择店，必居于此。
paragraphs.en: Three swindlers in a gang, having cheated three hundred taels together, wouldn’t split yet, kept it to set up a bigger cheat-booth, hoping for a big cheat. First they sent one across the province, to a prefecture two days from the provincial capital, spent seventy taels to buy a house; inside was an earth-storehouse; outside the wall they opened a guest inn. Another fifty taels to marry a wife, buy a maid, and buy a house slave. Several tens of taels more on hand to run the household. People saw the inn had a family, slaves and maids, food and use plentiful; many lodged there. This prefecture was near the provincial capital; in past years when the literary chancellor’s exam for the provincial examination wasn’t enough, they often transferred students from neighboring prefectures here for a joint exam, convenient for coming and going; every rich student choosing an inn would stay here.

paragraphs.zh: 壬子科六月，科期已迫，复调外两府生员来此选考。本店住建郡三个秀才，皆系巨富。一日，有客儒人品丰厚，衣冠鲜整，泊船城外，入此店来，密问店主曰：“你识科举秀才中有大家者乎？”店主曰：“我店中三位都富家，你问何干？”客儒曰：“有好事与他讲。”店主曰：“甚好事，何不对我说？”客儒曰：“你不在行，只好与秀才讲。”店主出，向三秀才曰：“此客先生问科举秀才何人最富，有好事对他说。我问他何事，又不肯言。列位试问其说何事。”三人共入叙礼，问曰：“老丈问富家，小弟等家皆万金，有何好事说？”客曰：“列位肯计较中否？”三秀才曰：“中都肯计较，兄有何门路？”客曰：“我亦不能为力，亦不识门路。但果肯计较者，各备银一千两，来此店对过封定，付还你收，自有指示的路。”三人约四日后家中取银来对，客儒辞去。三人密遣人跟随客去，见其下船，船中止一家人。归报如此，三秀才喜曰：“此必大主考的人，可信也。”店主出问：“适间说何事？”三秀才曰：“此未必然事，若事可成，自有大抬举你。”
paragraphs.en: In the sixth month of a renzi year, the exam date was pressing; they again transferred students from two outer prefectures here for selection. In this inn stayed three xiucai from Jian commandery, all very rich. One day a guest-scholar, substantial in manner, clothes fresh and neat, moored outside the wall, came into this inn, and secretly asked the innkeeper: “Do you know among the exam xiucai any from great families?” The innkeeper said: “The three in my inn are all rich; why do you ask?” The guest said: “I have a good matter to discuss with them.” The innkeeper said: “What good matter? Why not tell me?” The guest said: “You’re not in the trade; I can only speak with xiucai.” The innkeeper went out and told the three: “This guest-sir asked which exam xiucai is richest; he has a good matter to tell. I asked what, he wouldn’t say. You gentlemen try asking what he says.” The three went in, exchanged rites: “You asked about rich families; we younger brothers all have families of ten thousand taels; what good matter?” The guest said: “Would you gentlemen care to plan for passing?” The three said: “We all care to plan for passing; what opening do you have, brother?” The guest said: “I also can’t do anything, and don’t know an opening. But if you truly will plan, each prepare a thousand taels, come to this inn, check and seal it, give it back for you to keep; there will be a path indicated.” The three set four days to fetch silver from home to check; the guest-scholar left. The three secretly sent someone to follow; saw him go down to a boat, only one servant on the boat. They reported this; the three were glad: “This must be a man of the chief examiner; he can be trusted.” The innkeeper came out: “What did you just discuss?” The three said: “This isn’t yet a certain thing; if it can be done, we’ll greatly promote you.”

paragraphs.zh: 四日后，三家人都取银到。客儒应期来问，各答“银都齐备。”客曰：“今夜对明封定。”三秀才言：“银多夜间不便，明日入店主内庭去对。”客曰：“店主恐不密事，不知外客房中封更密。”三秀才曰：“明日临时相商。”客辞去。夜饭后，店主出曰：“列位与此客议封银事，客人难防。这门壁浅薄，若夜间统人来劫，可要提防。依我说，可藏入我城门内，你外间好心关防，可保安稳。”三秀才曰：“是也。”共将六皮箱银都寄入店主家内去。家主瞒过妻婢，将银尽从后门藏出，与棍伙夤夜逃去。唯嘱其妻曰：“明日三秀才问我，只说早间出去寻人，少刻即归。”
paragraphs.en: After four days, three servants all brought silver. The guest-scholar came as agreed and asked; each said “Silver is all ready.” The guest said: “Tonight we’ll check clearly and seal.” The three said: “There’s much silver; night is inconvenient; tomorrow go into the innkeeper’s inner court to check.” The guest said: “The innkeeper may not keep the matter secret; sealing in the outer guest rooms might be more secret.” The three said: “Tomorrow we’ll discuss at the time.” The guest left. After supper the innkeeper came out: “You gentlemen and this guest discussed sealing silver; the guest is hard to guard against. These door-walls are thin; if at night they bring people to rob, you must watch out. As I see it, you can hide it in my place inside the city gate; you keep good watch outside; that can be secure.” The three said: “Right.” Together they entrusted six leather cases of silver into the innkeeper’s house. The master, hiding it from wife and maid, took all the silver out the back door, and fled by night with the swindler gang. He only told his wife: “Tomorrow if the three xiucai ask for me, just say I went out early to find someone; I’ll be back shortly.”

paragraphs.zh: 次日，客儒欣欣喜色来对银。秀才曰：“银付店主收藏，今早出外，少待即归。”等到午间，店主不回。客辞归船。午后又遣家人来问，又以店主未归答之。至第三日午间，问店主妇取皮箱，妇答云：“并未见甚箱。”及出溪边寻客船，亦不见矣。再问店妇取，苦执未见。任入搜之，竟不见踪。问：“店主果何去？”妇云：“前夜已出，教我如此应你。”三人正慌。
paragraphs.en: The next day the guest-scholar came in good spirits to check silver. The xiucai said: “The silver was given to the innkeeper to keep; he went out this morning, will be back shortly.” They waited till noon; the innkeeper didn’t return. The guest went back to the boat. After noon they sent a servant to ask; again answered innkeeper not back. On the third day at noon they asked the innkeeper’s wife for the leather cases; she said: “I haven’t seen any cases.” They went to the creek to find the guest’s boat; it was also gone. They asked the wife again; she stubbornly insisted she hadn’t seen them. They searched inside as they liked; no trace. “Where did the innkeeper really go?” The wife said: “He left the night before last, told me to answer you this way.” The three were in a panic.

paragraphs.zh: 适此三棍脱得银去，已出境外。晚投宿一店，店主见其来晚，提其六箱皆重，疑是窃贼，明日将集众擒之。三棍闻其动静，次早天未明，只挑得四箱去，以二箱寄店。店主越疑是贼，出首于官。太府将银逐封开之，内封有一合同文书，称某人买举人者。太府提某生员到，不敢认。太府以甘言赚之，乃招认，即收入监。后又投分上解释，再骗去银四百两方免申道。又没入店主之屋，及官卖其妻婢，并箱内一千都追入库。彼四箱被棍挑去者，幸得落名，不受再骗。是府官亦一棍也。此为信店家一戒。
paragraphs.en: Just then these three swindlers, having stripped the silver, were already out of the territory. At night they lodged at an inn. The innkeeper saw they came late, lifted the six cases all heavy, suspected they were thieves; next day he would gather people to seize them. The three heard the stir, next morning before dawn only carried off four cases, left two at the inn. The innkeeper was more sure they were thieves, and reported to officials. The prefect opened the silver packet by packet; inside one seal was a contract document saying so-and-so was buying a juren. The prefect summoned that student; he dared not admit it. The prefect lured him with sweet words; he confessed, and was put in jail. Later he sought introductions to get out, and was cheated of another four hundred taels before they would refrain from reporting to the intendant. Also they confiscated the innkeeper’s house, and officially sold his wife and maid, and the thousand in the cases were all chased into the treasury. Those four cases the swindlers carried off luckily dropped the names, so they weren’t cheated again. Thus the prefectural official was also a swindler. This is a warning against trusting innkeepers.

paragraphs.zh: 按：店主有家眷，最可凭者。彼肯代藏银，孰不信之？谁知其妻妾皆买下以装棍棚者。彼骗得厚利，则弃此而去，别娶妻妾，享大富贵矣。以有眷属之店尚不可信，世路之险，一至于此！人若何不务实而可信棍以行险哉！
paragraphs.en: Note: An innkeeper with a family is the most trustworthy thing. If he’s willing to store silver for you, who wouldn’t believe? Who knew wife and concubine were all bought to set up the swindler-booth? Having cheated a thick profit, they abandon this and go, marry other wives, enjoy great wealth. Even an inn with dependents still can’t be trusted—the world’s roads are this dangerous! Why don’t people do solid work, instead trusting swindlers to walk a dangerous path?
